title: runtime traffic-fence upgrade: phased VPC data-plane rollout with telemetry-driven gating and fast rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: implement a reusable, low-risk upgrade mechanism for VPC/private data-plane/runtime that achieves zero-downtime for connected tenants by (1) applying a lightweight network "fence" around nodes undergoing upgrade, (2) progressively draining traffic using short-lived proxy sessions, (3) priming KV cache and synthetic warmers before shift, and (4) using telemetry-driven gating to automate rollback decisions. This ticket combines Terraform/IaC hooks, runtime sidecar proxy changes, orchestration controller logic, and an operator-runbook for emergency rollback. The solution must be compatible with Dedicated and Private modes and integrate with existing rollout controller policies.
acceptance_criteria: Can perform a staged upgrade on a 20-node VPC deployment without 5xx error rate increase >0.1% and p95 latency regressions >15%
Automated telemetry gates (error-rate, tail-latency, priming success) can halt or reverse rollout within 90s of breach
Rollback completes to previous runtime version and reinstates serving capacity within 3 minutes per affected slice with no data-plane session leaks
Terraform module provides an opt-in traffic_fence boolean and outputs hooks for pre-upgrade/success/post-rollback scripts
E2E integration test in CI simulates node upgrade with synthetic traffic and asserts no customer-visible 503s and consistent KV cache hits after priming
Runbook and on-call playbook checked into ops-runbooks with clear run/abort steps and required dashboards linked
tasks: Design: define traffic-fence semantics and API between orchestrator and sidecar proxy
IaC: add traffic_fence flag and pre/post lifecycle hooks to terraform/modules/vpc-runtime
Runtime: implement sidecar endpoint to accept 'fence' and 'unfence' transitions and drain connections gracefully
Orchestrator: add telemetry gate evaluator to rollout controller (error rate, p95, priming ack) with configurable thresholds
Priming: implement synthetic warmers that replay recent prefix traces to populate KV caches after upgrade
CI: add integration test that runs in local k8s and verifies rollback behavior
Observability: create dashboards and an alert rule for gating metrics, include runbook links
Security: KMS key use reviewed for any snapshots created during rollback snapshotting
Documentation: update Upgrade Playbook and Terraform module README
rollout_plan: 1) Toggle feature flag in a staging VPC and run full e2e tests. 2) Deploy sidecar and terraform module change to pilot tenant slice with traffic_fence=true. 3) Run priming warmers and validate KV hit-rate and synthetic probe success. 4) Start canary: fence node, drain sessions, upgrade runtime binary, unfence and run health probes. 5) Monitor gates for 15 minutes; if gates pass, continue to next slice with doubling batch size. 6) If any gate fires, orchestrator triggers automated rollback for slices in flight and unfences healthy nodes. 7) After full rollout, flip default in modules and announce via release notes.
rollback_plan: Two-tier rollback: automated and manual. Automated: orchestrator uses stored previous-version snapshot and signals sidecar to restore connection handoff, unfence nodes and reintroduce to LB. Manual: on-call runs 'rollback-fast' script that (a) fences affected slice, (b) reverts terraform to previous module image tag and applies, (c) runs cache-replay to rehydrate pre-upgrade state, (d) validates via smoke and synthetic probes. All rollback actions are recorded to audit logs and require a mandatory postmortem for any automated rollback event.
qa_plan: - Unit tests for sidecar fence API and orchestrator gate evaluator. - Integration test simulating 50 concurrent clients doing generation requests with KV cache validation. - Chaos test: interrupt priming process and assert orchestrator aborts upgrade on gate thresholds. - Performance test: verify p50/p95 token latency for a primed vs unprimed node.
risks: Priming may increase short-term token load causing false-positive gate failures if thresholds are not tuned
Network fence semantics could interact badly with existing connection pooling (envoy or lang-specific SDKs) requiring client-side timeouts adjustments
Terraform lifecycle hooks misconfiguration could leave nodes fenced without a safe rollback path if controller fails mid-step
Snapshotting previous versions for rollback may expose sensitive state if not encrypted and ACL'd correctly
notes: We want this feature to be opt-in per-tenant and default-off in terraform modules for first two releases
